sanskrit: tataḥ śarāḥ prāpatan rukmapuṅkhāḥ; śaktyaḥ prāsā musalāny āyudhāni paraśvadhās tailadhautāś ca khaḍgāḥ; pradīptāgrāḥ paṭṭiśās tomarāś ca
english: Then there rained down arrows with golden shafts, and spears, lances, clubs, and every kind of weapon, battle-axes and swords washed bright with oil, and flame-tipped pikes and javelins.

sanskrit: mayūkhinaḥ parighā lohabaddhā; gadāś citrāḥ śitadhārāś ca śūlāḥ gurvyo gadā hemapaṭṭāvanaddhāḥ; śataghnyaś ca prādurāsan samantāt
english: Iron-bound bludgeons gleaming with spikes, gaily-wrought maces and keen-edged spears, heavy clubs bound about with bands of gold, and śataghnīs appeared on every side.

sanskrit: mahāśilāś cāpataṃs tatra tatra; sahasraśaḥ sāśanayaḥ savajrāḥ cakrāṇi cānekaśatakṣurāṇi; prādurbabhūvur jvalanaprabhāṇi
english: Great boulders fell here and there by the thousand, charged with lightning and with thunderbolts, and discus-wheels rimmed with many hundred blades appeared, blazing with the splendour of fire.

sanskrit: tāṃ śaktipāṣāṇaparaśvadhānāṃ; prāsāsivajrāśanimudgarāṇām vṛṣṭiṃ viśālāṃ jvalitāṃ patantīṃ; karṇaḥ śaraughair na śaśāka hantum
english: That vast and blazing downpour as it fell—of spears and stones and battle-axes, of lances, swords, thunderbolts, lightnings, and mallets—Karṇa could not beat back with his floods of arrows.

sanskrit: śarāhatānāṃ patatāṃ hayānāṃ; vajrāhatānāṃ patatāṃ gajānām śilāhatānāṃ ca mahārathānāṃ; mahān ninādaḥ patatāṃ babhūva
english: Of horses falling, struck down by arrows, of elephants falling, smitten by thunderbolts, and of great chariot-warriors crushed by stones, a mighty din arose as they came toppling down.

sanskrit: subhīmanānāvidhaśastrapātair; ghaṭotkacenābhihataṃ samantāt dauryodhanaṃ tad balam ārtarūpam; āvartamānaṃ dadṛśe bhramantam
english: Battered on every side by Ghaṭotkaca with that fearful rain of weapons of every kind, the host of Duryodhana was seen reeling in distress, whirling about and spinning round.

sanskrit: hāhākṛtaṃ saṃparivartamānaṃ; saṃlīyamānaṃ ca viṣaṇṇarūpam te tv āryabhāvāt puruṣapravīrāḥ; parāṅmukhā na babhūvus tadānīm
english: Crying out in horror, surging back upon itself, dissolving away in utter dismay—yet those foremost of men, out of their noble temper, did not then turn their faces from the fight.

sanskrit: tāṃ rākṣasīṃ ghoratarāṃ subhīmāṃ; vṛṣṭiṃ mahāśastramayīṃ patantīm dṛṣṭvā balaughāṃś ca nipātyamānān; mahad bhayaṃ tava putrān viveśa
english: Beholding that most dreadful, terrible, demon-conjured downpour of mighty weapons as it fell, and seeing the floods of their troops struck down, a great fear entered your sons.

sanskrit: śivāś ca vaiśvānaradīptajihvāḥ; subhīmanādāḥ śataśo nadantyaḥ rakṣogaṇān nardataś cābhivīkṣya; narendrayodhā vyathitā babhūvuḥ
english: And jackals with tongues blazing like fire, howling by the hundred with dreadful cries, and the troops of demons roaring—seeing these, the warriors of the kings were filled with anguish.

sanskrit: te dīptajihvānanatīkṣṇadaṃṣṭrā; vibhīṣaṇāḥ śailanikāśakāyāḥ nabhogatāḥ śaktiviṣaktahastā; meghā vyamuñcann iva vṛṣṭimārgam
english: Those demons, with flaming tongues and mouths and sharp fangs, hideous, their bodies huge as mountains, ranging the sky with spears clutched fast in their hands, poured down their volleys as storm-clouds pour the rain.

sanskrit: tair āhatās te śaraśaktiśūlair; gadābhir ugraiḥ parighaiś ca dīptaiḥ vajraiḥ pinākair aśaniprahāraiś; cakraiḥ śataghnyunmathitāś ca petuḥ
english: Struck by them with arrows, spears, and pikes, with terrible maces and with blazing bludgeons, with thunderbolts, with tridents, with strokes of lightning, with discuses, and crushed by śataghnīs, the warriors fell.

sanskrit: huḍā bhuśuṇḍyo 'śmaguḍāḥ śataghnyaḥ; sthūṇāś ca kārṣṇāyasapaṭṭanaddhāḥ avākiraṃs tava putrasya sainyaṃ; tathā raudraṃ kaśmalaṃ prādurāsīt
english: Slings, bhuśuṇḍis, stone-balls, śataghnīs, and posts bound about with bands of black iron showered down upon your son's army, and so dread a confusion broke forth.

sanskrit: niṣkīrṇāntrā vihatair uttamāṅgaiḥ; saṃbhagnāṅgāḥ śerate tatra śūrāḥ bhinnā hayāḥ kuñjarāś cāvabhagnāḥ; saṃcūrṇitāś caiva rathāḥ śilābhiḥ
english: Their entrails spilled out, their heads shattered, their limbs broken, the warriors lay there strewn; horses were torn open and elephants smashed, and chariots ground to powder by the stones.

sanskrit: evaṃ mahac chastravarṣaṃ sṛjantas; te yātudhānā bhuvi ghorarūpāḥ māyāḥ sṛṣṭās tatra ghaṭotkacena; nāmuñcan vai yācamānaṃ na bhītam
english: Thus loosing that great rain of weapons, those night-prowlers, dread of form upon the earth, conjured into being there by Ghaṭotkaca's sorcery, spared neither the suppliant nor the frightened.

sanskrit: tasmin ghore kuruvīrāvamarde; kālotsṛṣṭe kṣatriyāṇām abhāve te vai bhagnāḥ sahasā vyadravanta; prākrośantaḥ kauravāḥ sarva eva
english: In that grim slaughter of the Kuru heroes, loosed by Time itself, in the ruin of the warriors, the Kauravas, broken, fled away all at once, every one of them, crying aloud.

sanskrit: palāyadhvaṃ kuravo naitad asti; sendrā devā ghnanti naḥ pāṇḍavārthe tathā teṣāṃ majjatāṃ bhāratānāṃ; na sma dvīpas tatra kaś cid babhūva
english: "Flee, O Kurus! There is no help in this! The gods with Indra slay us for the Pāṇḍavas' sake!"—and as those Bhāratas thus sank down, there was no island of refuge for any of them there.

sanskrit: tasmin saṃkrande tumule vartamāne; sainye bhagne līyamāne kurūṇām anīkānāṃ pravibhāge 'prakāśe; na jñāyante kuravo netare vā
english: While that tumultuous uproar went on, and the host of the Kurus, broken, melted away, the ordering of the ranks grown invisible, neither Kurus nor others could be told apart.

sanskrit: nirmaryāde vidrave ghorarūpe; sarvā diśaḥ prekṣamāṇāḥ sma śūnyāḥ tāṃ śastravṛṣṭim urasā gāhamānaṃ; karṇaṃ caikaṃ tatra rājann apaśyam
english: In that dreadful, boundless rout, all the quarters, as we gazed, appeared empty; and Karṇa alone, O king, I saw there, breasting that downpour of weapons with his chest.

sanskrit: tato bāṇair āvṛṇod antarikṣaṃ; divyāṃ māyāṃ yodhayan rākṣasasya hrīmān kurvan duṣkaram āryakarma; naivāmuhyat saṃyuge sūtaputraḥ
english: Then he veiled the sky with his arrows, battling against the demon's celestial sorcery; modest, performing a noble deed scarce to be done, the son of the charioteer was not bewildered in the fray.

sanskrit: tato bhītāḥ samudaikṣanta karṇaṃ; rājan sarve saindhavā bāhlikāś ca asaṃmohaṃ pūjayanto 'sya saṃkhye; saṃpaśyanto vijayaṃ rākṣasasya
english: Then in their fear all looked up toward Karṇa, O king—the men of Sindhu and the Bāhlikas alike—honouring his steadiness in the battle, even as they watched the demon prevailing.

sanskrit: tenotsṛṣṭā cakrayuktā śataghnī; samaṃ sarvāṃś caturo 'śvāñ jaghāna te jānubhir jagatīm anvapadyan; gatāsavo nirdaśanākṣijihvāḥ
english: A śataghnī fitted with wheels, hurled by the demon, slew all four horses together at once; sinking to their knees, they came down upon the earth, lifeless, their teeth and eyes and tongues all gone.

sanskrit: tato hatāśvād avaruhya vāhād; antarmanāḥ kuruṣu prādravatsu divye cāstre māyayā vadhyamāne; naivāmuhyac cintayan prāptakālam
english: Then, dismounting from the car whose horses were slain, his mind composed though the Kurus fled and his celestial weapon was being undone by sorcery, he was not bewildered, but pondered what the hour required.

sanskrit: tato 'bruvan kuravaḥ sarva eva; karṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā ghorarūpāṃ ca māyām śaktyā rakṣo jahi karṇādya tūrṇaṃ; naśyanty ete kuravo dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ
english: Then all the Kurus cried out, beholding Karṇa and that dread sorcery: "With the spear, O Karṇa, slay the demon now, this instant! These Kurus, these sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, are perishing!

sanskrit: kariṣyataḥ kiṃ ca no bhīmapārthau; tapantam enaṃ jahi rakṣo niśīthe yo naḥ saṃgrāmād ghorarūpād vimucyet; sa naḥ pārthān samare yodhayeta
english: What will Bhīma and Pārtha do to us then? Slay this demon who scorches us at midnight! He who delivers us from this battle of dread aspect—he it is who could make us face the Pārthas in the fight.

sanskrit: tasmād enaṃ rākṣasaṃ ghorarūpaṃ; jahi śaktyā dattayā vāsavena mā kauravāḥ sarva evendrakalpā; rātrīmukhe karṇa neśuḥ sayodhāḥ
english: Therefore slay this demon of dreadful form with the spear that was given you by Vāsava! Let not all the Kauravas, peers of Indra, with their warriors, O Karṇa, be lost at the onset of night!"

sanskrit: sa vadhyamāno rakṣasā vai niśīthe; dṛṣṭvā rājan naśyamānaṃ balaṃ ca mahac ca śrutvā ninadaṃ kauravāṇāṃ; matiṃ dadhre śaktimokṣāya karṇaḥ
english: Hard pressed by the demon there at midnight, and seeing, O king, his army perishing, and hearing the loud lament of the Kauravas, Karṇa set his mind upon loosing the spear.

sanskrit: sa vai kruddhaḥ siṃha ivātyamarṣī; nāmarṣayat pratighātaṃ raṇe tam śaktiṃ śreṣṭhāṃ vaijayantīm asahyāṃ; samādade tasya vadhaṃ cikīrṣan
english: Wrathful as a lion and beyond all bearing, he would brook no thwarting of him in that battle; and so he took up that supreme, victory-giving, irresistible spear, resolved to slay the demon.

sanskrit: yāsau rājan nihitā varṣapūgān; vadhāyājau satkṛtā phalgunasya yāṃ vai prādāt sūtaputrāya śakraḥ; śaktiṃ śreṣṭhāṃ kuṇḍalābhyāṃ nimāya
english: That spear, O king, which had been laid by for years on end, kept honoured for the slaying of Phalguna in battle—the supreme spear that Śakra gave to the son of the charioteer in exchange for his earrings—

sanskrit: tāṃ vai śaktiṃ lelihānāṃ pradīptāṃ; pāśair yuktām antakasyeva rātrim mṛtyoḥ svasāraṃ jvalitām ivolkāṃ; vaikartanaḥ prāhiṇod rākṣasāya
english: That spear, licking the air and blazing bright, bound with snares like the very Night of the Ender, like the sister of Death, like a flaming meteor—Vaikartana hurled it at the demon.

sanskrit: tām uttamāṃ parakāyāpahantrīṃ; dṛṣṭvā sauter bāhusaṃsthāṃ jvalantīm bhītaṃ rakṣo vipradudrāva rājan; kṛtvātmānaṃ vindhyapādapramāṇam
english: Seeing that supreme, body-shattering weapon blazing in the charioteer's son's hand, the demon fled away in terror, O king, having made himself the size of a Vindhya foothill.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā śaktiṃ karṇabāhvantarasthāṃ; nedur bhūtāny antarikṣe narendra vavur vātās tumulāś cāpi rājan; sanirghātā cāśānir gāṃ jagāma
english: Beholding the spear poised in the crook of Karṇa's arm, the spirits of the air cried out, O lord of men; tumultuous winds blew, O king, and lightning with a crash of thunder struck the earth.

sanskrit: sā tāṃ māyāṃ bhasma kṛtvā jvalantī; bhittvā gāḍhaṃ hṛdayaṃ rākṣasasya ūrdhvaṃ yayau dīpyamānā niśāyāṃ; nakṣatrāṇām antarāṇy āviśantī
english: Blazing, it burned that sorcery to ashes, and cleaving deep through the demon's heart, it soared aloft, shining in the night, passing in among the spaces of the stars.

sanskrit: yuddhvā citrair vividhaiḥ śastrapūgair; divyair vīro mānuṣai rākṣasaiś ca nadan nādān vividhān bhairavāṃś ca; prāṇān iṣṭāṃs tyājitaḥ śakraśaktyā
english: Having fought with manifold and wondrous volleys of weapons—celestial, human, and demonic—the hero, roaring his many dreadful roars, was made to yield up his dear life by the spear of Śakra.

sanskrit: idaṃ cānyac citram āścaryarūpaṃ; cakārāsau karma śatrukṣayāya tasmin kāle śaktinirbhinnamarmā; babhau rājan meghaśailaprakāśaḥ
english: And this further marvel, of wondrous form, he wrought as a deed for the destruction of his foes: in that hour, his vitals pierced through by the spear, he shone, O king, like a mountain wreathed in cloud.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣād apatad gatāsuḥ; sa rākṣasendro bhuvi bhinnadehaḥ avākśirāḥ stabdhagātro vijihvo; ghaṭotkaco mahad āsthāya rūpam
english: Then from the sky there fell, his life gone out, that lord of demons, his body cleft, upon the earth—head downward, his limbs grown rigid, his tongue lolling out—Ghaṭotkaca, having taken on a vast form.

sanskrit: sa tad rūpaṃ bhairavaṃ bhīmakarmā; bhīmaṃ kṛtvā bhaimaseniḥ papāta hato 'py evaṃ tava sainyekadeśam; apothayat kauravān bhīṣayāṇaḥ
english: That son of Bhīmasena, dread in his deeds, having made his shape fearful and huge, fell down; and even slain, he thus crushed a whole quarter of your army, striking terror into the Kauravas.

sanskrit: tato miśrāḥ prāṇadan siṃhanādair; bheryaḥ śaṅkhā murajāś cānakāś ca dagdhāṃ māyāṃ nihataṃ rākṣasaṃ ca; dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭāḥ prāṇadan kauraveyāḥ
english: Then, mingled with their lion-roars, the kettledrums and conches, tabors and war-drums sounded; and seeing the sorcery burned away and the demon slain, the Kauravas, rejoicing, shouted aloud.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇaḥ kurubhiḥ pūjyamāno; yathā śakro vṛtravadhe marudbhiḥ anvārūḍhas tava putraṃ rathasthaṃ; hṛṣṭaś cāpi prāviśat svaṃ sa sainyam
english: Then Karṇa, honoured by the Kurus as Śakra was by the Maruts at the slaying of Vṛtra, mounted the chariot beside your son who stood upon it, and rejoicing entered his own army.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca haiḍimbaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā vikīrṇam iva parvatam pāṇḍavā dīnamanasaḥ sarve bāṣpākulekṣaṇāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing the son of Hiḍimbā slain and strewn upon the ground like a fallen mountain, the Pāṇḍavas were all downcast in spirit, their eyes blurred with tears.

sanskrit: vāsudevas tu harṣeṇa mahatābhipariplutaḥ nanāda siṃhavan nādaṃ vyathayann iva bhārata vinadya ca mahānādaṃ paryaṣvajata phalgunam
english: But Vāsudeva, overwhelmed with a mighty joy, roared a roar like a lion, as though to dismay the foe, O Bhārata; and having let forth that great roar, he embraced Phalguna.

sanskrit: sa vinadya mahānādam abhīśūn saṃniyamya ca nanarta harṣasaṃvīto vātoddhūta iva drumaḥ
english: Having sounded that great cry and drawn in the reins, he danced, wrapped about with joy, like a tree shaken by the wind.

sanskrit: tato vinirbhrāmya punaḥ pārtham āsphoṭya cāsakṛt rathopasthagato bhīmaṃ prāṇadat punar acyutaḥ
english: Then, whirling about and clapping Pārtha again and again upon the arms, Acyuta, standing in the body of the chariot, shouted aloud once more in his delight.

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭamanasaṃ jñātvā vāsudevaṃ mahābalam abravīd arjuno rājan nātihṛṣṭamanā iva
english: Knowing that the mighty Vāsudeva was glad at heart, Arjuna spoke, O king, like one whose own heart was not much gladdened.

sanskrit: atiharṣo 'yam asthāne tavādya madhusūdana śokasthāne pare prāpte haiḍimbasya vadhena vai
english: "This great rejoicing of yours today is out of place, O Madhusūdana, when a fresh occasion for grief has come upon us through the slaying of Hiḍimbā's son.

sanskrit: vimukhāni ca sainyāni hataṃ dṛṣṭvā ghaṭotkacam vayaṃ ca bhṛśam āvignā haiḍimbasya nipātanāt
english: Our armies have turned their faces from the field, seeing Ghaṭotkaca slain, and we ourselves are sore distressed at the fall of Hiḍimbā's son.

sanskrit: naitat kāraṇam alpaṃ hi bhaviṣyati janārdana tad adya śaṃsa me pṛṣṭaḥ satyaṃ satyavatāṃ vara
english: Surely the cause of this cannot be a slight one, O Janārdana; therefore, being asked, tell me now the truth of it, O best of the truthful.

sanskrit: yady etan na rahasyaṃ te vaktum arhasy ariṃdama dhairyasya vaikṛtaṃ brūhi tvam adya madhusūdana
english: If this be no secret of yours, you should declare it, O subduer of foes; tell me now, O Madhusūdana, the cause of this break in your composure."

sanskrit: samudrasyeva saṃkṣobho meror iva visarpaṇam tathaital lāghavaṃ manye tava karma janārdana
english: "Like a churning of the ocean, like a shifting of Meru, so do I count this light-hearted conduct of yours, O Janārdana."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca atiharṣam imaṃ prāptaṃ śṛṇu me tvaṃ dhanaṃjaya atīva manasaḥ sadyaḥ prasādakaram uttamam
english: Vāsudeva said: Hear from me, O Dhanaṃjaya, the cause of this great joy that has come upon me—a thing that on the instant brings the highest gladness to the heart.

sanskrit: śaktiṃ ghaṭotkacenemāṃ vyaṃsayitvā mahādyute karṇaṃ nihatam evājau viddhi sadyo dhanaṃjaya
english: Now that this spear has been spent upon Ghaṭotkaca, O greatly resplendent one, know Karṇa, O Dhanaṃjaya, to be as good as slain in battle this very moment.

sanskrit: śaktihastaṃ punaḥ karṇaṃ ko loke 'sti pumān iha ya enam abhitas tiṣṭhet kārttikeyam ivāhave
english: Were the spear yet in Karṇa's hand, what man in the world is there who could stand before him in battle, as before Kārttikeya himself?

sanskrit: diṣṭyāpanītakavaco diṣṭyāpahṛtakuṇḍalaḥ diṣṭyā ca vyaṃsitā śaktir amoghāsya ghaṭotkace
english: By good fortune his armour was taken from him, by good fortune his earrings were carried off, and by good fortune his unfailing spear has been spent upon Ghaṭotkaca.

sanskrit: yadi hi syāt sakavacas tathaiva ca sakuṇḍalaḥ sāmarān api lokāṃs trīn ekaḥ karṇo jayed balī
english: For had he still his armour and his earrings as well, the mighty Karṇa, alone, could have conquered the three worlds, gods and all.

sanskrit: vāsavo vā kubero vā varuṇo vā jaleśvaraḥ yamo vā notsahet karṇaṃ raṇe pratisamāsitum
english: Neither Vāsava, nor Kubera, nor Varuṇa the lord of waters, nor Yama would dare to close with Karṇa in battle.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvam āyamya bhavāṃś cakraṃ vāhaṃ sudarśanam na śaktau svo raṇe jetuṃ tathāyuktaṃ nararṣabham
english: Though you drew the Gāṇḍīva and I bore the discus Sudarśana, we two could not have conquered in battle that bull among men so armed.

sanskrit: tvaddhitārthaṃ tu śakreṇa māyayā hṛtakuṇḍalaḥ vihīnakavacaś cāyaṃ kṛtaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ
english: But for your good, by Śakra, through a stratagem, this conqueror of hostile cities was robbed of his earrings and stripped of his armour.

sanskrit: utkṛtya kavacaṃ yasmāt kuṇḍale vimale ca te prādāc chakrāya karṇo vai tena vaikartanaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Because he cut away that armour and those two bright earrings of his and gave them to Śakra, Karṇa is therefore remembered as Vaikartana, 'the Cutter.'

sanskrit: āśīviṣa iva kruddhaḥ stambhito mantratejasā tathādya bhāti karṇo me śāntajvāla ivānalaḥ
english: Like an angry venomous serpent stilled by the power of a spell, so does Karṇa appear to me today, like a fire whose flame is quenched.

sanskrit: yadā prabhṛti karṇāya śaktir dattā mahātmanā vāsavena mahābāho prāptā yāsau ghaṭotkace
english: From the very day, O mighty-armed one, that the spear was given to Karṇa by the great-souled Vāsava—the spear that has now been spent upon Ghaṭotkaca—

sanskrit: kuṇḍalābhyāṃ nimāyātha divyena kavacena ca tāṃ prāpyāmanyata vṛṣā satataṃ tvāṃ hataṃ raṇe
english: —obtaining it in exchange for his earrings and his celestial armour, the bull Karṇa, once he had it, deemed you slain in battle for good and all.

sanskrit: evaṃ gate 'pi śakyo 'yaṃ hantuṃ nānyena kena cit ṛte tvā puruṣavyāghra śape satyena cānagha
english: Yet even so, this man can be slain by no one else but you, O tiger among men; I swear it by my truth, O sinless one.

sanskrit: brahmaṇyaḥ satyavādī ca tapasvī niyatavrataḥ ripuṣv api dayāvāṃś ca tasmāt karṇo vṛṣā smṛtaḥ
english: Devoted to the brahmins, truthful in speech, given to austerity, steadfast in his vows, and compassionate even toward his foes—therefore is Karṇa remembered as Vṛṣa, the bull of virtue.

sanskrit: yuddhaśauṇḍo mahābāhur nityodyataśarāsanaḥ kesarīva vane mardan mattamātaṅgayūthapān vimadān rathaśārdūlān kurute raṇamūrdhani
english: Greedy for battle, mighty-armed, his bow ever bent and ready, like a lion in the forest crushing the lords of rutting elephant-herds, he leaves the tiger-warriors of the chariots stripped of their pride in the forefront of the fight.

sanskrit: madhyaṃgata ivādityo yo na śakyo nirīkṣitum tvadīyaiḥ puruṣavyāghra yodhamukhyair mahātmabhiḥ śarajālasahasrāṃśuḥ śaradīva divākaraḥ
english: Like the sun gone to mid-heaven, he cannot be looked upon, O tiger among men, by the great-souled foremost of your warriors—his thousand rays the web of his arrows, like the day-maker in autumn.

sanskrit: tapānte toyado yadvac charadhārāḥ kṣaraty asau divyāstrajaladaḥ karṇaḥ parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān so 'dya mānuṣatāṃ prāpto vimuktaḥ śakradattayā
english: As a rain-cloud at the end of the hot season, he pours down his streams of arrows; Karṇa, a thundercloud of celestial weapons, is like Parjanya laden with rain—yet today he is brought down to mere mortal estate, parted from the gift of Śakra.

sanskrit: eko hi yogo 'sya bhaved vadhāya; chidre hy enaṃ svapramattaḥ pramattam kṛcchraprāptaṃ rathacakre nimagne; hanyāḥ pūrvaṃ tvaṃ tu saṃjñāṃ vicārya
english: There is but one way for his slaying: in a moment of opening, you yourself unheedless while he is heedless, when he has come to grief and his chariot-wheel has sunk in the earth—then you must strike him down first, taking thought and choosing your moment.

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdhaś cedirājo mahātmā; mahābalaś caikalavyo niṣādaḥ ekaikaśo nihatāḥ sarva eva; yogais tais tais tvaddhitārthaṃ mayaiva
english: Jarāsaṃdha, and the king of the Cedis, that great soul, and the mighty Ekalavya the Niṣāda—all of these, one by one, were slain by me alone, by this device or that, for your good.

sanskrit: athāpare nihatā rākṣasendrā; hiḍimbakirmīrabakapradhānāḥ alāyudhaḥ parasainyāvamardī; ghaṭotkacaś cograkarmā tarasvī
english: And other lords of demons too were slain—chief among them Hiḍimba, Kirmīra, and Baka—and Alāyudha, the crusher of hostile hosts, and the swift Ghaṭotkaca, dreadful in his deeds.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca katham asmaddhitārthaṃ te kaiś ca yogair janārdana jarāsaṃdhaprabhṛtayo ghātitāḥ pṛthivīṣvarāḥ
english: Arjuna said: How, and by what devices, O Janārdana, were Jarāsaṃdha and the other lords of the earth made to be slain for our good?

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca jarāsaṃdhaś cedirājo naiṣādiś ca mahābalaḥ yadi syur na hatāḥ pūrvam idānīṃ syur bhayaṃkarāḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: Jarāsaṃdha, and the king of the Cedis, and the mighty son of the Niṣāda—had they not been slain before, they would now be a source of terror.

sanskrit: suyodhanas tān avaśyaṃ vṛṇuyād rathasattamān te 'smābhir nityasaṃduṣṭāḥ saṃśrayeyuś ca kauravān
english: Suyodhana would surely have sought out those foremost of chariot-warriors, and they, forever hostile to us, would have taken the side of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: te hi vīrā mahātmānaḥ kṛtāstrā dṛḍhayodhinaḥ dhārtarāṣṭrīṃ camūṃ kṛtsnāṃ rakṣeyur amarā iva
english: For those great-souled heroes, masters of weapons and steadfast in fight, would have guarded the whole host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons like immortals.

sanskrit: sūtaputro jarāsaṃdhaś cedirājo niṣādajaḥ suyodhanaṃ samāśritya taperan pṛthivīm imām
english: The son of the charioteer, and Jarāsaṃdha, and the king of the Cedis, and the son of the Niṣāda—leaning upon Suyodhana, they would have scorched this earth.

sanskrit: yogair api hatā yais te tān me śṛṇu dhanaṃjaya ajayyā hi vinā yogair mṛdhe te daivatair api
english: Hear from me, O Dhanaṃjaya, the devices by which they were slain; for without such stratagems they were unconquerable in battle even by the gods.

sanskrit: ekaiko hi pṛthak teṣāṃ samastāṃ suravāhinīm yodhayet samare pārtha lokapālābhirakṣitām
english: Each one of them, alone and singly, O Pārtha, could have given battle to the whole host of the gods, guarded though it be by the World-Guardians.

sanskrit: jarāsaṃdho hi ruṣito rauhiṇeyapradharṣitaḥ asmadvadhārthaṃ cikṣepa gadāṃ vai lohitāmukhīm
english: For Jarāsaṃdha, enraged and provoked by the son of Rohiṇī, hurled, to slay us, a mace with a blood-red mouth.

sanskrit: sīmantam iva kurvāṇāṃ nabhasaḥ pāvakaprabhām vyadṛśyatāpatantī sā śakramuktā yathāśaniḥ
english: Cleaving as it were a parting through the sky, with the radiance of fire, it was seen falling like the thunderbolt loosed by Śakra.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ dṛṣṭvaiva gadāṃ rohiṇinandanaḥ pratighātārtham astraṃ vai sthūṇākarṇam avāsṛjat
english: Seeing that mace come hurtling down, the son of Rohiṇī, to beat it back, let fly the weapon called Sthūṇākarṇa.

sanskrit: astravegapratihatā sā gadā prāpatad bhuvi dārayantī dharāṃ devīṃ kampayantīva parvatān
english: Checked by the force of that weapon, the mace fell down upon the earth, rending the goddess Earth and seeming to make the very mountains tremble.

sanskrit: tatra sma rākṣasī ghorā jarā nāmāśuvikramā saṃdhayām āsa taṃ jātaṃ jarāsaṃdham ariṃdamam
english: There a dreadful demoness, swift in her might, Jarā by name, had joined together at his birth that subduer of foes, Jarāsaṃdha.
